The dog gets expensive-looking organic, grain-free, high-protein food, while the owner eats cheap instant noodles at the table. The joke is the dietary double standard between pampering the pet and neglecting her own nutrition.

From a distance, the man's arm markings look like sleeve tattoos, but the close-up reveals they are just dense hair patterns. The humor comes from mistaking natural body hair for intentional body art.
She carefully applies SPF sunscreen, prioritizing protection from the sun, but then rides a scooter with her helmet dangling unused behind her, ignoring more serious safety protection.

The left panel highlights a “No Sugar” Diet Cola, suggesting a calorie-conscious choice, but the right panel shows it paired with a huge burger and fries. The humor is the selective dieting: avoiding sugar while eating an extremely indulgent meal.

The left panel suggests the important clothing label is the size tag, but the right panel replaces that focus with a dangling price/barcode tag. The joke is that shoppers may care about cost before fit.
The left panel suggests a clean victory through the referee raising a boxer’s glove, but the right panel reveals the “winner” is battered and bruised, making the triumphant pose look hollow.

The left calendar marks a vacation from the 20th–26th with a beach note, but the right menstrual calendar shows those same dates as menstruation days. The planned holiday is contradicted by an inconvenient biological schedule.

The woman confidently chooses chopsticks over the fork and knife, suggesting sophistication or skill. But the close-up shows the food trembling and falling as she awkwardly struggles to use the chopsticks.

The toy/plane box in the back seat is carefully strapped in with a seatbelt, while the actual passenger sits beside an unused belt. The joke is that safety is applied to the toy instead of the person.

The left panel shows a normal pedestrian signal with a red standing figure, while the right panel shows that red signal stopping crossing at an empty, carless intersection. The humor is the pointless obedience to traffic control when there is no visible danger.

The gloved worker carefully prepares a taco, suggesting food hygiene, but then the same glove handles cash from a customer. The cleanliness meant to protect the food is undermined by touching dirty money.
In the left panel, the dog walkers and dogs are calmly separated with their own leashes. In the right panel, their paths have crossed and the leashes form a tangled knot around the dogs.

The left panel shows a window insect screen meant to keep bugs out, but the right panel shows mosquitoes already inside, biting a person and leaving red marks. The protection exists, but it has failed.
The box advertises a 256GB phone, but the phone’s storage screen shows only 235.35GB available. The joke is the missing advertised space caused by built-in system usage or storage overhead.

The left panel presents a majestic king before his castle, suggesting royal grandeur. The right reveals the castle’s WC as a tiny exposed wall-mounted outhouse where the king sits, reducing the “throne” to a literal toilet.

The steering wheel in the left panel is polished with sparkle marks, but the right panel reveals the rest of the dashboard screen/console is grimy and spotted. The joke is selective cleanliness: only the wheel is immaculate.

The left panel shows a man sweating on a rowing machine, simulating strenuous boat-rowing exercise. The right panel contrasts this with him easily riding in a motorboat, where real boating requires no rowing effort at all.
The left panel shows a pigeon gracefully flying, but the right shows a pigeon walking on the street beside a large vehicle wheel, making its ability to fly seem foolishly underused and risky.

The left panel shows flip-flops decorated with a tropical beach scene, but the right panel shows that feet cover most of the design when worn. The appealing artwork becomes largely invisible in actual use.
The man holds a crossed-out “ABORTION” sign while the woman faces a positive pregnancy test; later she is left holding the baby as he walks out. His pro-life advocacy ends when responsibility begins.

The left door sign says “OPEN,” matching the man entering through an opened door. On the other side, the sign reads “CLOSE,” turning a normal open/closed business sign into an absurd door-motion instruction.
The hand offers a cat treat in the YES panel, implying the cat will take the snack. In the BUT panel, the cat bites the person's finger instead while the treat remains untouched in the palm.

The left panel shows cars neatly separated into lanes with straight directional arrows, while the right panel shows pedestrians with arrows crisscrossing chaotically. It jokes that vehicle traffic is disciplined, but foot traffic lacks comparable order.

The sealed cup’s lid shows an appealing picture of ingredients, but when peeled back the inside reveals a flat, unappetizing slab of food. The humor comes from the packaging’s visual promise being exposed as misleading.
The left panel presents a tender surprise gift labeled for Bob, suggesting generosity. The right panel reveals the gift is being paid for with Bob’s own credit card, undermining the romantic gesture.

The left panel presents a colorful bouquet as a cheerful decorative object, while the right places the same bouquet before a gravestone. The humor comes from flowers symbolizing both celebration and mourning depending on context.

The left panel presents a flat, toned stomach while standing, but the right panel shows the same midsection folding and bulging when seated. The joke is that body “perfection” changes with posture and circumstance.

The left panel shows people playing with abundant vegetables as eye masks, while the right panel shows a rabbit crying in a garden full of empty holes. The joke contrasts playful food abundance with deprivation for the animal that would actually need it.

The left panel shows an underwater scene full of colorful fish, while the right panel shows the same view crowded by swimmers’ legs and bodies instead. The joke is that the expected marine life has been replaced by masses of tourists.

The left panel shows pumpkin seeds being thrown away while carving a pumpkin, but the right panel shows a man eating store-bought “pumpkin seeds” beside the finished jack-o’-lantern. The humor is wasting the same food he later buys and snacks on.

The left panel shows a male performer adored by excited female fans, suggesting conventional celebrity heartthrob appeal. The right panel undercuts that expectation by showing him affectionately holding hands with another man.
The left panel shows a man rescuing a puppy from flames, suggesting compassion and protection. The right panel undercuts this by showing the same dog later tied up on a chain outside a doghouse.

The left panel romanticizes autumn leaves with a person posing dreamily under a maple leaf. The right panel undercuts that idyllic nature image by showing the same leaf-covered ground as a dog-filled park, including a dog squatting to poop.

The left panel presents a drinking-water station, emphasized by the sign and dispenser, but the right panel reveals the cup holder is essentially empty, making the water available yet impractical to drink.

The left panel presents a perfect 5.0 rating with five stars, implying strong quality. The right panel undercuts it by revealing the score is based on only one review, making the perfection statistically weak and misleading.

The left panel markets shiny soccer cleats as a “LIMITED EDITION” performance item; the right shows a player wearing them while the shot flies wide of the goal. The joke is that exclusivity and style do not translate into skill.

The left panel presents an exercise bike as fitness equipment, but the right panel shows the same bike buried under clothes, a tote bag, and slippers, functioning more like household storage than something used for exercise.

The left panel shows a FastPass ticket promising quicker entry, but the right panel shows the FastPass entrance crowded while the regular entrance is empty. The supposed shortcut becomes the slower line.

The viewer raises the TV volume to hear quiet dialogue, shown by the high volume bars. But when the scene switches to action, the sound becomes painfully loud, making him plug his ear and shake the room.

The left panel shows a neatly decorated Christmas tree from the man’s viewing angle; the right reveals the other side is tangled with ribbon and lights. The humor is that the attractive holiday display only works from one direction.
The left panel shows a marked bicycle lane, suggesting cyclists have a dedicated space. The punchline is that the cyclist instead rides in the regular traffic lane among cars and a bus.

The left panel shows a relaxation kit full of bath-specific items like bath salts and bubble bath, but the right panel reveals only a shower stall. The joke is that the soothing bath kit is impractical when there is no bathtub.

A phone advertises a large “MEGA CAMERA” module, but its photo gallery is filled with mundane utility shots like meters, receipts, parking spots, price tags, and food. The joke is advanced camera hardware being used for low-key documentation.

The message says “text me when you get home,” implying concern, but the person is asleep while the phone on the nightstand is muted/do-not-disturb. The joke is that the caring request is undercut by not being available to receive the reply.

The left panel shows the object wrapped with “CAUTION FRAGILE” tape, implying it must be handled delicately. The right panel reveals it is a sturdy punching dummy meant to take hits, making the warnings absurd.

The left panel piles up urgent demands—a boiling pot, boss call, doorbell, and burning iron—but the right panel shows the person motionless with a sleeping cat on their lap. The joke is that pet comfort overrides all the chores and pressure.

The left panel presents a reusable bottle with a recycling symbol as an eco-friendly choice. The right panel undercuts this by showing it being refilled from a disposable plastic bottle, making the green gesture depend on the waste it rejects.

She recoils from a small medical syringe in the left panel, hiding her face, but in the right panel she calmly endures needles for cosmetic work: a lip procedure and a tattoo machine. The same needle shifts from terrifying to fashionable.

The left panel presents a complete robot, but the right panel reveals a human head on the same robotic body while he holds the robot head like a mask. The “robot” is actually a person in a mechanical suit.

The left panel presents a camouflaged car as stylishly hidden; the right shows it blending into roadside greenery so well that another car crashes into it. The concealment becomes a visibility hazard.

The waiter presents a large covered serving dish, suggesting a substantial gourmet meal. The reveal is an oversized plate with decorative sauce but only a tiny morsel of food, mocking fancy dining portions.
The left panel suggests someone is turning on a sink faucet to wash their hands, but the right panel reveals that the same setup triggers an overhead shower, soaking the person at the sink.

The left panel shows an elderly academic with broad traditional expertise but almost no TikTok skill. The right panel gives the microphone-filled spotlight to someone whose chart shows only TikTok expertise, mocking how online fame can outweigh knowledge.

With the light off, shadows on the man's torso make him look muscular and defined; when the bulb is on, the same body appears flat and untoned. The joke is that darkness creates a flattering physique that daylight removes.

The left panel presents a fully equipped recording studio with instruments and a mixing board, but the right panel reveals music being assembled from digital tracks and waveform blocks. The joke is elaborate production reduced to clicking software loops.

The left panel presents spotless, sparkling sneakers as if they are perfectly clean. The right panel reveals that when one shoe comes off, the hidden white sock is dirty, contradicting the pristine exterior.

The left panel presents a luxury pen in a case with a $2,065 price tag, implying superior writing. The right panel shows the same expensive pen producing a sloppy signature, undercutting the idea that cost improves penmanship.

The left panel presents a human winner wearing a “Miss Universe” sash, but the right panel reveals actual alien contestants from the universe. The joke is that a supposedly universal beauty title is absurdly Earth-centered.

The left panel shows ordinary potato peeling with a hand peeler, but the right turns the peel into a rhythmic-gymnastics ribbon and the peeler into the apparatus handle. The joke is the absurd elevation of a mundane kitchen task into performance art.

The left panel presents a blue pocket square as a normal suit accessory. The right panel reveals the “pocket square” is actually a disposable face mask tucked into the breast pocket, turning a protective pandemic item into fashion.

The close-up makes the woman's tiptoed heel seem romantically close to a man's sneaker. The full view reveals the sneaker belongs to a very short man standing between her and the taller man she is actually toasting.

The left panel makes the person's rounded shirt look like an overweight belly. The right panel reveals the bulge is actually a large shell-like natural protrusion behind the shirt, reversing the initial assumption.

The left panel frames the man like a triumphant winner crossing a ribbon under confetti, but the right panel reveals the “finish line” is simply him getting out of bed. The joke inflates an ordinary daily act into a victory celebration.

The left panel suggests a normal single earbud in use; the right reveals both earbuds worn, but one side shows a low battery icon while music notes appear on the other, making listening a one-sided concert.

The woman refuses a COVID vaccine in the left panel, shown by her crossed hands and the labeled vial, but accepts a hyaluronic acid injection into her lips in the right panel. The humor is her selective fear of medical injections.

The left panel makes the woman’s foggy glasses look like they are obscuring her eyes. In the right panel, after she removes them, her actual squinting eyes look similarly blank, making the glasses seem like an illusion of open eyes.

The left panel frames the man cutting a ribbon like a grand ceremonial event. The right panel reveals he is actually in a mundane queue area, having cut through the line barriers instead of participating in a celebration.

The left panel shows a pizza seemingly loaded with many sausage slices. The right panel reveals the apparent abundance is a peelable top layer, hiding one large sausage sheet underneath instead of generous individual toppings.

The left panel presents a polished man in a clean suit holding champagne, suggesting refined celebration. The right panel contradicts this with the same man disheveled, stained, and drunk with a bottle, revealing the messy reality behind the decorum.

The map search treats “Carefree Childhood” like a reachable destination from the current location. The BUT panel shows a GPS route stretching impossibly into the distance, making nostalgia look like a navigable place even though the past cannot be physically reached.

The left panel shows a drink marketed as organic, gluten-free, non-GMO and 100% natural, implying health-conscious choices. The right panel reveals the same kind of hand smoking a cigarette, undercutting that concern for health.
The left side shows normal use: a pedestrian on stairs and a cyclist on a bike path. The right side reverses this logic, with a cyclist awkwardly on stairs and a pedestrian walking in the bike lane.

The left close-up implies someone is driving a Porsche, highlighted by the logo on the steering wheel. The right reveals it is only a detached steering wheel being tossed like a frisbee in a park, mocking the illusion of luxury.

The left panel looks like a normal suited man taking an elevator mirror selfie. The right panel reveals the “elevator” is an exposed, tiny exterior lift/platform, making the calm corporate selfie absurdly unsafe and deceptive.

The left panel shows an action camera enjoying a surfer’s adventurous wave scene, while the right panel reveals a bulky surveillance camera stuck in a warehouse, drooling as if fantasizing about that life.

In the left panel, the man bends under a limbo bar like a dance move; in the right, the same bend is used to slip beneath an airport queue barrier and bypass waiting passengers. The joke turns a playful skill into rude line-cutting.

The man laughs and points at a TV remote sealed in protective plastic, implying it is ridiculous. But he then travels with a suitcase similarly wrapped in protective plastic, showing selective judgment about protection.

The left panel suggests making a normal single cup of tea from a tea bag. The right panel exaggerates this by using one tea bag and kettle to fill a whole stack of mugs, stretching one serving absurdly far.
The can’s front advertises “NO SUGAR,” but the other side reads “NO SUGAR? NO PROBLEM THERE’S A LOT OF IT,” undercutting the healthy claim with a hidden sugary truth.

The left panel suggests the child is giving a bedridden elderly man a glass of water to drink. In the right panel, he instead uses the water with a paintbrush and palette, turning caregiving into watercolor painting.

The YES panel shows a hockey player in a “Climate Change Cup” uniform, but the BUT panel shows him using a hockey stick on a grassy golf course instead of ice. The joke is that warming has turned ice hockey into golf.

The left panel presents a #1 trophy as a glorious personal victory, while the right panel shows identical trophies being mass-produced and boxed in a factory. The prestige of winning is undercut by its ordinary manufacturing process.

The left panel shows a thick designer wallet covered in “BRAND” logos, suggesting luxury and abundance. The right panel reveals the wallet opened with no cash or cards inside, undercutting the status implied by the expensive accessory.

The tattoo declares “My Life... My Rules...,” suggesting total personal freedom. The right panel counters with law, the constitution, and science books, implying life is governed by external social and natural rules.

The left panel shows an ordinary bird sitting on a glowing streetlamp. The right panel flips this by making pigeons themselves have glowing bulb-like bodies, as if the lamps have turned into flying birds.

The money “CHANGE” sign suggests a currency exchange, and the man enters with one modest dollar-chain necklace. In the BUT panel, he exits overloaded with dollar-symbol chains, turning “change” into an absurd fashion upgrade.
The close-up makes the chips, dip, and pretzel snacks look like ordinary human party food, but the wider view reveals the diner is a dog at the table, turning snack time into a dog's lunch.

The many shoes by the door suggest a crowded gathering, but the room contains only one man and a giant many-legged creature. The punchline is that the “guest list” implied by the shoes is actually one centipede-like guest.

The left panel shows a sweaty man carefully stacking money into a pyramid labeled “BUDGET,” implying disciplined financial planning. The right panel undercuts this with a crane smashing a piggy bank and scattering cash, suggesting reckless spending destroys the plan.

The left panel shows plastic straws crossed out as an environmental concern, while the right shows a large cup of disposable sampling swabs and a test kit. The joke is society scrutinizes straws while accepting other single-use medical plastics.

The left panel frames a luxury-looking “BRAND” badge as if the car is prestigious. The right panel reveals the same car’s side is old and rusty, so the status symbol clashes with the vehicle’s actual shabby condition.
In the first panel the men seem to have distinctive hairstyles; in the second, they politely lift those hairstyles like hats, revealing bald heads and turning hair into removable wigs.
The fox-shaped mug looks charming, but when the woman drinks from it, its pointed ear presses into her eye and makes her cry. The cute design is painfully impractical.

The hat appears to have a transparent checkerboard background in the PNG viewer, but when placed on the person, that checkerboard remains as an opaque square obscuring their face instead of disappearing.

Indoors, the man listens to “Birdsongs—Sounds of the Forest,” but while walking among real trees and birds, he replaces nature with a rap song. His listening choices invert what each environment naturally offers.
The shirt proudly reads “NONBINARY,” but the shopping interface still requires choosing between only male and female gender icons. The supposedly inclusive product is sold through a binary system.
The man prominently identifies as “VEGAN” while eating lettuce, but the close-up shows him biting a hangnail—humorously consuming a piece of his own body despite his plant-only principle.
The man receives a festive birthday welcome with confetti, but afterward he alone sweeps up the party debris while the other guests socialize behind him.
A rider crashes headfirst into a pole and lies unconscious, yet the responder only scans for COVID and appears satisfied by the “NO COVID” result, ignoring the obvious traumatic injury.
The businessman presents a selectively enlarged rebound as a dramatic rise, while the full chart reveals that the highlighted movement sits at the end of a long overall decline.

The woman appears to pray devoutly before the Buddha, but the wider view reveals her photographing the pose for a social-media post labeled “#praying.” Her apparent piety is staged for online display.

From above, the four hair patterns all look like stages of balding, but the frontal view reveals that similar outlines can belong to baldness or dramatic mohawks. The joke depends on how perspective radically changes the interpretation.
The hand intends to pull the cord plug from the adapter, as indicated by the left-pointing arrow, but instead pulls the entire adapter from the wall and exposes its prongs.
A single tiny pill is contrasted with an enormous, densely printed medicine-instruction leaflet. The absurd imbalance suggests that understanding the medication is more overwhelming than taking it.

She exercises on a stair-climbing machine, yet presses the elevator button to reach the gym instead of taking the adjacent real stairs. The avoidance of ordinary steps contradicts her deliberate indoor stair workout.

The parody account openly says its posts are usually taken from and credited to the original owner, yet the original owner has blocked that account. Attribution does not prevent conflict over unauthorized reuse.
From the front, the ice cream cone appears full and intact, but the reverse view reveals that most of its center is missing, exposing a deceptive shell-like presentation.
The artist’s song is titled “I Don’t Care,” yet he anxiously bites his nails while watching its declining statistics. His visible concern contradicts the indifference he claims.
A plush cat bed is provided, but the cat chooses to sleep awkwardly draped over its outer edge instead of inside it. The humor comes from the cat rejecting the obviously comfortable space.
The sealed box promises “INVISIBLE TAPE,” but opening it reveals a plainly visible white roll. The product name contradicts the tape’s obvious physical visibility.
The left panel shows a neatly arranged picnic platter, while the right shows the food blown off its tray and scattered across the blanket, revealing the windy reality of an exposed picnic spot.

As a child, he happily imagines driving in his toy car, but as an adult he is miserable behind the wheel, trapped in heavy traffic with a congested route displayed. The dream of driving becomes a frustrating reality.
At 23:59 the app shows 9,999 steps and only one remaining, but at 00:00 the daily counter resets, making the newly taken step count as just 1 and leaving 9,999 again.
The cozy self-embrace in the left panel suggests comfort, but the right reveals an irritating clothing tag scratching the person's neck, turning that comfort into a small agony.
The account has only 1,053 followers despite following 5,467 others, suggesting that mass-following people has failed to produce equivalent followbacks or social influence.

The left carton offers a convenient screw cap, while the right relies on a large, awkwardly unfolded traditional pouring spout. The two incompatible opening designs make the carton’s intended pouring method confusing.
The free scissors contrast with identical scissors sealed in packaging whose dotted cut line calls for scissors to open it. The tool needed to access the product is trapped inside the package.
The pedestrian signal shows green, but the wide view reveals an empty crosswalk while a car waits nearby. The walk phase is active for pedestrians who are not there.
The playlist is labeled “music i love,” yet the listener’s finger immediately presses the next-track button, suggesting they do not want the current supposedly loved song.
The woman’s cheerful smile appears positive, but the close-up reveals that repeated smiling leaves prominent wrinkles around her eye and cheek, making the smile double-edged.
A huge wall-mounted television promises an immersive viewing experience, but the movie appears only as a narrow strip across the middle, leaving much of the big screen unused.

The zipper pulls appear securely locked together with a combination lock, yet the right panel shows the zipper teeth separating and leaving the bag open anyway. The elaborate lock therefore provides only an illusion of security.
The shoes are advertised at a steep discount from $120 to $54.99, but the size menu reveals that only the extreme sizes 35 and 47 are available. The bargain has a restrictive catch.

The sofa looks perfectly placed and pristine in the YES panel, but the BUT panel reveals the movers damaged walls, shattered glass, and littered the floor to get it there. The successful setup came at a destructive cost.

From outside, the woman appears to occupy a cozy, attractive café window; from her seat, however, she looks directly onto a dilapidated building and trash-strewn vacant lot. The appealing spot depends entirely on which side of the window is viewed.
The “Secret Beach” sign promises a hidden, secluded destination, but the beach is prominently marked and crowded with visitors. Its publicity and popularity undermine its supposed secrecy.

The real fireplace on the left contains logs but no flame, while the television on the right displays a roaring virtual fire. Technology imitates the warmth that the unused physical fireplace could provide.
A person swats a tiny mosquito on their white shirt, but the attempt leaves an absurdly huge blood-colored splatter, making the hasty solution far worse than the original problem.
The king-size label promises abundant sleeping space, but the person’s clothes, laptop, and other clutter consume much of the oversized bed, leaving little usable room.
The anti-aging skincare regimen promises youthful looks, but the 2-hour sleep record and ashtray amid discarded cans reveal habits that undermine health and accelerate aging.
The man is angered by another person's music in the left panel, yet blasts music from his own car in the right. He condemns the same noisy behavior when someone else does it but embraces it himself.

The bodybuilder projects a fierce persona with a flaming skull and “KILL” shirt, yet chooses whey protein in childishly cute flavors labeled “yummy yummy choco,” “teddy vanilla,” and “strawberry unicorn.”
Despite having an elaborate multi-level cat tree, the cat chooses to sit in a plain cardboard box instead. The contrast humorously shows the simple box beating the fancy pet furniture.

The colorful fireworks look festive in the YES panel, but the BUT panel reveals several frightened pets hiding under furniture from the noise. The spectacle enjoyed by people becomes a source of fear for animals.
The open cup displays intricate latte art, but a takeaway lid immediately covers and hides it. The decorative work becomes invisible to the person drinking the coffee.

Despite having many proper dog toys, the puppy ignores them and chooses to chew a household slipper instead. The humor comes from its preference for the forbidden, ordinary object over the abundant options.

The person wears an extremely thick puffer jacket for the snowy weather, yet pairs it with heavily ripped jeans that expose their legs to the cold. Fashion undermines the outfit’s practical winter warmth.
A woman tells the superhero-fantasy fan to “Stop living in a fantasy world,” yet she enthusiastically embraces astrology, tarot, and zodiac imagery—another fantasy-based worldview.
A blank canvas in a traditional studio filled with classical sculptures becomes an anime character portrait, humorously contrasting fine-art expectations with cartoon imagery.

The power bank is connected to rescue a nearly dead phone, but the right panel reveals that the backup battery is itself nearly empty. The matching low-battery icons turn the supposed solution into another problem.

The boy affectionately stands beside and pets a cow in the left panel, but in the right panel he happily eats a likely beef burger. His apparent compassion for the animal conflicts with consuming it as food.

The YES panel presents stacks of real banknotes as wealth, while the BUT panel reduces that apparent fortune to worthless Monopoly money beside the game board. The joke contrasts monetary appearance with actual value.
The dashboard provides a clear reverse-camera display, yet the driver ignores it and turns around to look backward manually, making the technology redundant.

She presents her ballet visit as “#cultural” while watching the dancers, but in the auditorium she is actually asleep. Her cultivated public image contradicts her genuine engagement with the performance.

The close-up makes the man seem threatened by aggressive dogs, but the wider view reveals he is approaching their shelter to put money in its donation box. His generosity is unseen and misjudged by the dogs.
A nail clipper is readily available, but the person ignores it and bites their nails with their teeth instead. The humor comes from choosing the crude method despite having the proper tool.
The card promises that grand dreams of travel and luxury can come true, but inside it offers only a five-dollar bill—comically modest support for such ambitions.

The long ponytail initially suggests a full head of hair, but the wider rear view reveals a large bald patch hidden above it. The hairstyle creates a misleading impression depending on the viewing angle.

The glamorous, distinctly dark-haired father and blonde mother contrast with their baby, whose sparse hair and oddly mature-looking face do not resemble the expected blend of either parent. The humor frames inheritance as an unpredictable genetic roulette.

The man modestly appears to select food at the buffet, but the close-up reveals his plate absurdly overloaded with bread and pastries. The excessive pile turns ordinary buffet choice into comical gluttony.
She draws a blank when asked for presidents’ names, yet readily fills a long list with the names of his exes, humorously showing selective memory for relationship trivia over basic history.
The band advertises a “WORLD TOUR,” but the map highlights tour stops in only the United States and a small part of Western Europe, making the supposed worldwide scope comically limited.
The entrance advertises the property as a five-star hotel, but its online listing shows only a 3.7 rating. The lofty official image clashes with guests’ less impressive assessment.

The opaque container appears full of fresh strawberries on top, but the transparent view reveals discolored, spoiled berries hidden underneath. The attractive upper layer deceptively conceals the poor-quality contents.

The slogan says “Beauty is Inside,” but the woman sits at a vanity applying makeup to improve her outward appearance. The same slogan reflected beside her makes her cosmetic routine especially ironic.
An empty shopping basket is readily available, yet the shopper ignores it and awkwardly balances a large pile of groceries in her arms.

The sleek mirror uses a touch-sensitive power button, but touching it leaves a conspicuous fingerprint smudge around the illuminated control. Its high-tech interface therefore makes the mirror visibly dirty.
A woman calmly enjoys coffee by the café window, but her supposedly pleasant view is dominated by a dog defecating outside. The refined café moment clashes with the crude street scene.
The green pedestrian signal says it is safe to walk, but a bus blocks the zebra crossing. The permitted route is therefore physically unusable.
The ergonomic chair is designed to support proper posture, yet the woman sits hunched forward without using its backrest. Her visibly curved spine negates the chair’s intended benefit.

The player proudly displays “GOD IS GREAT,” implying faith in divine support, but the final scoreboard shows his blue team losing 0–3. The decisive defeat undercuts the celebratory religious confidence.
The plane ticket costs only $50, while the phone shows a $68 taxi fare to the airport. The humor is that reaching the flight costs more than the flight itself.
Although a proper trash bin is available, a person presses discarded gum onto a nearby railing instead. The humor comes from choosing lazy littering over the obvious disposal option.

A snowplow creates a convenient cleared route, but the people deliberately trudge and play through the deep snow instead of using it. Their enjoyment contradicts the practical purpose of clearing the path.

The phone is advertised as “ULTRA SLIM,” but its limited practicality forces the user to attach a bulky external battery and charging cable, making the overall setup much thicker and cumbersome.
After exerting herself lifting weights, the woman uses the elevator and presses floor 2 rather than taking the stairs, humorously avoiding a small amount of everyday exercise.
The robot vacuum makes the floor sparkle clean, but its own dusty surface must be wiped by a human finger. The labor-saving cleaner ironically creates another cleaning task.
The woman sunbathes in a square-mesh cover-up, then reveals that the garment has left a matching checkerboard tan pattern across her skin instead of an even tan.
The sealed Caesar salad advertises only 290 calories, suggesting a healthy meal, but opening it reveals a large dressing tub and abundant croutons that undermine that low-calorie impression.

The Fight Club shirt condemns working hated jobs to buy unnecessary things, yet its wearer is shown doing an ordinary office job at a computer. His behavior undercuts the rebellious belief displayed on his clothing.
The left panel shows a hand pulling one tissue normally, while the right reveals that a whole clump of tissues has come out together instead.
A message says “You are cute,” but the phone’s dark screen reflects the recipient as an ape-like face, humorously undermining the compliment through their self-perception.
The fitness watch celebrates 10,000 steps, but the wearer is a prisoner pacing inside a small barred cell. His impressive milestone is humorously reduced to walking repeatedly toward nowhere.
The rider joyfully speeds downhill on the sled in the YES panel, but the BUT panel reveals the exhausting reverse journey: walking uphill while dragging the same sled behind.

The computer desktop is meticulously organized into labeled folders, while the physical desk around it is buried under scattered papers, dishes, and other clutter. The humor comes from digital organization coexisting with real-world disorder.
The man appears to wake to a pleasant sunrise, but the raised tail and rear of his cat reveal the much less pleasant sight greeting him in bed.
The package window appears filled by a neat, substantial salmon fillet, but opening it reveals a much smaller, irregular piece positioned to create that illusion.

The man calmly regards an X-ray of severely damaged teeth, yet sweats while using a magnifying glass to inspect a minor issue on his car. His concern is absurdly focused on the car rather than his health.
A person joins a 28-person group chat, then immediately presses the muted-notifications bell. Joining suggests participation, while silencing the chat ensures they can ignore it.
The left cup features an elaborate latte-art leaf, but in the right panel a person immediately stirs the coffee, dissolving the carefully made design into meaningless swirls.
The left panel presents a clean, inviting picnic with cheese, while the right reveals the food and blanket overrun by ants and flies. The pleasant outdoor meal becomes an insect banquet.
The empty tub offers a clear mountain view through the windows, but once the woman bathes, steam fogs the glass and obscures the scenery she would enjoy.
The glowing office windows make an attractive nighttime backdrop for the woman’s photo, but the other panel reveals that the lights come from employees still working late inside.

The close-up makes the bicycle lock appear securely attached to a post, but the wider view reveals it merely loops around the front wheel without securing the bike to the post. The lock therefore does little to prevent theft.
The package prominently advertises vegan mayonnaise, but a hand pours it onto a meat steak. The vegan label clashes with the clearly non-vegan food choice.

The person displays a “VEGAN” tattoo, but the tattoo ink is shown being produced from animal bones. Their attempt to express vegan values is therefore undermined by the material used to create the tattoo.

The first truck cruises at 80 km/h, but another truck overtakes it at only 81 km/h while it remains beside the 80 km/h truck. The tiny 1 km/h advantage turns overtaking into an absurdly slow highway drama.
Clothing makes the visible neck, hand, and knee tattoos suggest extensive hidden body art. Once undressed, his torso is blank, revealing that tattoos exist only where the outfit exposed skin.

A woman arrives at the Halloween party dressed as Barbie, only to discover that all the other guests are wearing virtually identical pink Barbie costumes. Her seemingly distinctive costume becomes a uniform.
A print-and-copy shop issues a queue ticket whose text is faded and barely legible. The business specializing in printing cannot clearly print its own ticket.

A person deliberately covers the laptop webcam with a finger for privacy, yet leaves the prominent front-facing camera on their phone uncovered. The selective precaution creates a technology privacy paradox.
The bald man looks unhappy beside men with hair, but smiles in the pool because their swim caps make everyone appear equally bald.
The cap’s brim could shade the wearer’s eyes, but he wears it backward and must use his hand to block the sun instead.
The patio umbrella appears positioned to shade the table and chairs, but the right panel reveals its shadow falling far off to the side, leaving the seating exposed.
The man displays a snake tattoo on his arm, suggesting bravery or affinity for snakes, yet panics atop a chair when confronted by a real snake.
The elaborate dual-monitor gaming rig and powerful PC contrast with the same person's sparse sleeping arrangement: a bare mattress on the floor in an otherwise empty room.

The peaceful cuddling couple suggests that sleeping in an embrace is cozy and romantic, but the same couple is shown drenched in sweat beside a high thermometer, revealing how unbearably hot it becomes.
The inviting breakfast tray on a neatly made bed contrasts with the stained pillows and crumb-covered bedding afterward. The luxury of breakfast in bed creates an unpleasant mess.
The masked protester displays an “ACAB” sign, yet then dials 112 for emergency assistance, implicitly relying on the authorities they condemn.

The fortune teller’s crystal ball promises knowledge of the “FUTURE,” but when customers seek betting, lottery, and investment predictions, it displays “Unknown error.” Her supposed foresight fails precisely when useful predictions are requested.
The neatly spread blanket in the YES panel makes the bed look orderly, but the lifted cover in the BUT panel reveals twisted, chaotic sheets underneath.

The hotel room promises a tranquil ocean view through its window, but the wider scene reveals a gigantic wave about to engulf the beachfront hotel. The serene coastal setting is therefore a perilous paradise.

The painter creates a “SAVE OUR EARTH” mural while leaving an overturned paint bucket, spilled paint, and debris in the surrounding grass. Their environmental message is contradicted by their own pollution.

The moon appears enormous above the buildings, but on the smartphone screen it becomes a tiny dot despite photographing the same scene. The humor reflects how phone cameras fail to capture the Moon’s apparent scale.

The colorful fruit chart and matching legend clearly distinguish seven categories, but the grayscale printout renders the donut segments and legend swatches nearly identical, making the data unreadable.
The opaque cup appears to contain a full drink, but the transparent view reveals it is packed almost entirely with ice, leaving only a small amount of beverage.
Bob promotes free speech as a civil right, yet his “Blocked People (1273)” list prevents a huge number of people from commenting on his posts. His behavior contradicts his stated principle.
A cart overflowing with groceries needs cargo room, but the car’s open trunk is occupied by a large speaker system, leaving nowhere to load them.

The left panel quotes the warning that rich people cannot attain eternal life, while the right shows an ornately dressed, apparently wealthy religious leader teaching that same camel-and-needle doctrine. His institutional splendor contradicts the lesson against wealth.
The unfinished to-do list suggests plans still awaiting completion, but the deceased person being zipped into a body bag has reached an unexpected final deadline.
After sending a resume, the person immediately rejects an incoming call from an unknown number, potentially hanging up on the very employer they hope will respond.

The woman publicly signals love for nature with hashtags such as “#lovenature,” but her bare feet are shown trampling the flowers. Her behavior physically undermines the environmental affection she professes.

The camera promises 16 million colors, but the photographer’s real surroundings are rendered gray and choked by industrial smoke. Its vast color capability is ironically wasted in a polluted, colorless world.
The outlet is awkwardly mounted beneath an overhang, while the bulky charger’s shape and elevated prongs make the apparently available connection difficult or impossible to use.
The man politely insists “LADIES FIRST,” but walking behind her leaves him engulfed in the vapor from her device. His chivalrous gesture creates an unpleasant physical consequence.

A seated passenger tries to enjoy a peaceful read, but another passenger stands so close that their backside intrudes directly into her space. The serene reader-and-book image contrasts with the rude, cramped reality of public transit.
The left panel emphasizes the cup’s large handle, designed for easy gripping, but the man in the right panel ignores it and awkwardly grasps the cup’s body while drinking.
A man offering “FREE HUGS” stands ignored, while a crowd gathers around a router labeled “FREE WIFI.” The contrast mocks modern society’s preference for digital connectivity over human connection.

The customer receives luxurious barbershop treatment with drinks, gaming, and attentive service, but the close-up reveals an absurdly uneven, mangled haircut. The premium experience contradicts the barber’s poor result.
People happily admire a “Blue Cat,” but recoil when the same breed is labeled “Russian Blue Cat.” Their affection is overridden by geopolitical prejudice attached to the word “Russian.”
The advice to “DRINK MORE WATER,” illustrated by a filled glass, is undercut by the long queue at the restroom, showing the inconvenient consequence of increased hydration.
The bottle promises premium mineral water, but the ice added to it is made with ordinary tap water. As the ice melts, it undermines the drink's supposed premium purity.
The singer appears huge and close on the venue screen, but the wide view reveals that the actual performer is tiny and far from the audience.

The reusable bag’s leaf logo and “eco bag” label signal environmental responsibility, but the same bag is filled with plastic bottles, detergent packaging, and other disposable containers. The supposedly green choice contrasts with the shopper’s plastic-heavy purchases.

The man proudly displays an extensive collection of Air Jordan sneakers, but when he actually plays basketball, his shot misses the hoop completely. His enthusiasm for basketball branding contrasts with his lack of skill on the court.

A monitor prominently advertised as 4K is used to display a very low-resolution, pixelated retro game from an old console. The contrast humorously makes the advanced display technology seem unnecessary.

He impatiently waits on hold with a call center while his phone reveals 53 unanswered chats from friends asking why he is silent. He demands responsiveness from customer service yet ignores everyone contacting him.
The man is about to enjoy a slice of pizza, but his dog's large, pleading eyes turn the simple meal into a guilt-inducing burden of pet ownership.
From outside, the bus wheel and partially visible passengers make the seating appear normal; the cutaway reveals that the wheel housing forces one passenger into a cramped, knees-up position.
The sign promises “Buy 2 Get 1 Free,” but the sale bin contains only two items, making it impossible to obtain the advertised third item.
The hiker anticipates a vivid summit panorama with sunshine and a rainbow, but reaches the peak only to find the view obscured by gray clouds and fog.
The woman appears committed to her salad in the YES panel, but in the BUT panel she reaches across to take fries from her companion’s burger-and-fries meal, undermining her healthy choice.

The user creates an extremely complex password that earns a “Strong” rating, but by sign-in time must click “Forgot Password?” The security strength that makes the password desirable also makes it impossible to remember.

She spends time photographing the meal while it is steaming hot, as shown by the phone and red thermometer, but only begins eating after the food has become icy cold, marked by snowflakes and the blue thermometer.
She hides her face in shame beside a handbag stamped “FAKE,” yet the right panel marks her cosmetic features and body with repeated “FAKE” labels, exposing her hypocrisy about artificiality.

The cyclist rides only 6.23 km, yet drives 97.45 km with the bicycle mounted on the car, presumably just to reach the cycling location. The journey to exercise is vastly longer than the exercise itself.
The empty parking space initially seems like a lucky find, but the birds perched directly overhead and droppings below reveal why nobody parked there.

One remote conveniently controls the TV in the YES panel, but the BUT panel shows a hand confused by a cluttered array of nearly indistinguishable remotes. The abundance of controls undermines technological convenience.

The prominent cross tattoo suggests the woman’s religious devotion, while the right panel reveals her performing provocatively on a stripper pole. The humor comes from the perceived clash between pious symbolism and behavior conventionally labeled sinful.
The romantic “wish you were here” message sounds like an invitation to an idyllic place, but the sender is actually texting while sitting on a toilet with his pants down.
The closet’s hangers are completely empty, while the clothes are piled over a chair instead. The humor lies in having proper storage available but ignoring it for an improvised clothes rack.
The pristine snow and glowing winter sunset suggest an idyllic landscape, but the closer view reveals an ugly, muddy path covered in melting slush and puddles.
The Wi-Fi demands a long, complex password, while the bank account is protected by the easily guessed PIN “1234.” The security priorities seem absurdly reversed.
The “VIEW ONCE” option promises an ephemeral message, but the visible “Screenshot” control shows that its contents can still be captured and preserved.

A normal chair is presented as the obvious place to sit, but the woman instead perches on a bathroom counter beside the sink to take a mirror selfie. The humor comes from choosing an awkward bathroom surface over actual seating.
A club rejects a man wearing shorts under a no-shorts sign, yet admits women in equally short skirts. The dress code is enforced inconsistently based on gender.

A supposedly life-saving first-aid video shows urgent emergency care, but playback is delayed by a fast-food advertisement labeled “Ad 1 of 2.” The commercial interruption absurdly undermines the urgency of the lesson.

The boy is frustrated by abstract equations and geometric diagrams in class, yet happily engages with the same curves and shapes when they appear as skateboard ramps. Math becomes appealing when embodied in skateboarding.
The open umbrella keeps the person dry in the rain, but once folded, its trapped water drips onto their trousers and shoe, creating the very wetness it was meant to prevent.
The players exuberantly celebrate an apparent goal, including one doing a handstand, but the VAR display announces “NO GOAL” because of offside. Their jubilation is therefore premature.

A man works remotely on a laptop at a sunny beach, suggesting an ideal mobile office, but the screen shows only 3% battery and two minutes remaining. The lack of practical power undermines the idyllic setup.
The digital E-Ticket shown in the YES panel is unnecessarily printed onto a large sheet of paper in the BUT panel, defeating the convenience and purpose of an electronic ticket.

The orange car initially approaches in the empty lane beside a queue, but then cuts diagonally into that queued lane near the split. The humor is its lane choice serving as a shortcut rather than patient merging.
The elegant long, pointed manicure looks attractive on its own, but those same sharp nails make a massage uncomfortably scratchy, as shown by the red marks on the client’s skin.

The left panel presents the blue check badge as one person’s proud distinction, while the right reveals that nearly everyone—even a dog and a trash can—has one. Its ubiquity makes the supposed honor meaningless.
The ticket assigns Row 3, Seat 18, but the attendee enters from the opposite aisle and must squeeze across a packed row to reach the highlighted seat beside the far-right aisle.
From the front, the cube appears perfectly solved because its visible face is entirely red; the angled view reveals that only this surface matches while the other faces remain scrambled.

The man readily hands cash to a waiter clearing his restaurant plate, but offers nothing when his partner performs the same task at home. The identical service exposes his double standard about tipping and appreciation.
A neat row of rental scooters suggests convenient travel, but the path ahead is riddled with large puddles and broken, uneven pavement, making scooter riding impractical.

The woman cleans around the man while he eats a crumbly snack at home, but in the car she becomes the messy eater herself, scattering pastry crumbs everywhere. Their roles in the cleanliness conflict are humorously reversed.
A tulip bouquet is treated as a romantic gift in the YES panel, while the BUT panel shows a dog lifting its leg among the same flowers, turning veneration into desecration.
The sale advertisement insists it is valid “ONLY TODAY,” but the online-shop post is labeled “Posted 3 days ago.” The stale post makes the supposed one-day urgency logically impossible.

Women's beauty standards demand three precise body measurements (90-60-90), while men's are reduced to a single height requirement above 180 cm. The contrasting charts humorously expose gendered and uneven expectations of attractiveness.
The left panel appears to show a comfortably charged phone, but the right reveals that green battery is only preserved in an old screenshot while the phone’s actual battery is nearly empty.
A standard vegetable peeler is shown as simple and useful, but the knobby, irregular ginger root beside it is nearly impossible to peel neatly with that tool.
The suitcase is designed to roll easily on its tiny wheels, but the uneven cobblestone pavement would make pulling it awkward and jolting.
The left panel promises a hearty, ingredient-filled bowl of shrimp soup, while the right isolates the meager reality: just four shrimp tails. The sparse catch undercuts the soup’s rich appearance.

The map and its many pins show that the tourist has visited destinations worldwide, yet the labeled vacation photos from Egypt, Portugal, Turkey, and elsewhere all feature virtually the same poolside pose.
The woman feeds her dog expensive organic, high-protein food while she eats cheap instant noodles herself. The contrast humorously shows greater dietary care for the pet than for its owner.

The woman poses glamorously on the yacht under carefree hashtags, but the reality shows her hunched over and vomiting from seasickness. Her supposedly picture-perfect yacht day is physically miserable.
From a distance, the man's arms appear covered in ornate sleeve tattoos, but the close-up reveals that the patterns are merely dense, swirling arm hair.

She carefully applies high-SPF sunscreen, yet rides a scooter bareheaded while her helmet sits unused behind her. The minor protection from sunlight contrasts with ignoring the much more essential crash protection.

The “NO SUGAR” diet cola suggests calorie-conscious restraint, but it accompanies an enormous cheese-laden burger and a large serving of fries. The tiny dietary concession is humorously overwhelmed by the indulgent meal.
The clothing size is hidden on a small inner label, while the price is displayed prominently on a large dangling tag, emphasizing what retailers prioritize showing shoppers.

The raised glove initially signals a victorious boxer, but the reveal shows the winner covered in bruises, cuts, and blood. His triumphant pose contrasts humorously with the severe damage hidden behind the referee.
The planned beach holiday is circled for dates 20–26, but the menstrual calendar marks those exact dates with blood drops. The anticipated vacation is inconveniently synchronized with menstruation.
The woman confidently chooses chopsticks instead of the available fork, but the right panel shows her struggling to grip the food as the chopsticks awkwardly cross and snag it.
The toy box is securely strapped into the back seat, while the man beside it leaves his own seat belt unused. He protects the toy from a crash but not himself.
The pedestrian signal orders people to stop, yet the wider view reveals a completely empty road and unused crosswalk. The safety restriction feels absurd because there is no traffic to wait for.

The vendor wears gloves to hygienically prepare a taco, but then uses the same gloved hand to accept dirty cash. The supposed food-safety measure therefore risks transferring contamination from money to food.
The left panel shows three dogs walking separately on orderly leashes, while the right reveals that their crossing paths have knotted all the leashes together around the dogs.
The window screen appears designed to keep insects out, yet several mosquitoes are inside, with one actively biting the person. The barrier provides only an illusion of protection.
The box advertises 256 GB of phone storage, but the phone reports only 235.35 GB available. The humor comes from the substantial portion of advertised capacity that is already missing before use.
The regal, crowned king posed before his castle is undercut by the same monarch using a tiny exposed WC built into the castle wall—an unexpectedly humble alternative throne.

The steering wheel is polished to a sparkling shine, while the nearby touchscreen remains covered in fingerprints and smudges. The humor comes from selectively cleaning one frequently touched surface but neglecting another.
The man strains on an indoor rowing machine, yet when actually traveling on water he uses an outboard motor instead of rowing. Simulated boating demands exercise while real boating is effortless.

The left pigeon effortlessly flies, while the right pigeon walks beside a vehicle wheel despite having wings. The contrast humorously shows a city bird choosing pedestrian travel over its natural ability.
The flip-flops display a vivid tropical paradise when empty, but the wearer's feet cover nearly all of that decorative design once they are worn.

The man loudly opposes abortion while the woman faces a positive pregnancy test, but after the baby is born he walks out with his luggage, abandoning them. His proclaimed conviction disappears when parenthood requires personal responsibility.
The man passes through a door marked “OPEN,” but on the other side faces a closed door marked “CLOSE,” turning ordinary status signs into contradictory instructions about operating the doors.
The cat appears to consider the treats offered in the open palm, but instead of taking them, it bites the person's finger. The humor comes from the cat choosing the hand over the obvious bait.

Cars follow straight, orderly directional arrows in defined road lanes, while pedestrians on the footpath follow numerous curving, intersecting arrows. The contrast humorously portrays vehicle traffic as disciplined and pedestrian movement as chaotic.

The lid’s colorful food illustration makes the cup appear appetizing, but peeling it back reveals an unappealing pink mass inside. The attractive packaging creates a misleading illusion about the actual meal.
The lovingly wrapped present is labeled for Bob, but the giver secretly pays for it using Bob's own credit card. The supposed act of generosity therefore leaves the recipient buying his own gift.
The cheerful bouquet displayed decoratively in a vase becomes a grave offering beside a tombstone, contrasting flowers as symbols of both joy and mourning.

Standing upright makes the woman’s abdomen appear flat, while sitting causes the same body to fold and protrude. The contrast humorously reveals how posture reshapes the appearance of an supposedly “flawless” figure.

People casually use abundant vegetables as beauty masks and playthings, while a tearful rabbit sits before empty garden holes with no food. The humor contrasts frivolous abundance with deprivation on the other side.
The inviting reef is full of colorful fish in the YES panel, but the same underwater view in the BUT panel is crowded with swimmers instead, leaving no fish visible.
The man discards the fresh seeds while carving a pumpkin, yet later snacks on packaged pumpkin seeds. The humor comes from throwing away the same food he then buys and eats.

The male star is adored by excited female fans onstage, but the second panel reveals him affectionately holding hands with another man. The humor contrasts his public appeal to women with his private romantic orientation.
The man rescues and cradles the puppy amid flames, suggesting compassion, but afterward the dog is left sadly chained outside. The rescue from danger leads only to another form of confinement.

The left panel romanticizes lying in autumn leaves, while the right reveals that dogs routinely squat or lift their legs among those same leaves. The idyllic contact with nature is undercut by the leaves' likely use as a canine toilet.
The drinking-water station promises accessible water, but the adjacent cup dispenser is completely empty, leaving users with no practical way to drink it.
The impressive 5.0 score and five stars appear to signal proven excellence, but the right panel reveals that the rating is based on only one review, making it statistically unconvincing.

The limited-edition cleats are presented like a prized performance item, but the player wearing them kicks the ball outside the goalpost. Their exclusivity clearly does not guarantee skill or effectiveness.
The YES panel shows a clean exercise bike ready for workouts, while the BUT panel shows the same equipment buried under clothes and a bag, functioning as a makeshift rack instead.
The FastPass ticket promises quicker entry, but the FastPass entrance has a long queue while the regular entrance is empty. The supposed shortcut therefore creates more waiting.

The viewer raises the volume to hear quiet dialogue, but the following action scene becomes so deafening that he plugs his ears. The uneven sound mix turns one comfortable volume setting into two opposite problems.
The Christmas tree looks neatly decorated from the front, but its hidden reverse side is a chaotic tangle of ribbon and lights. The man decorated only the visible half.
A clearly marked bicycle lane is empty while the cyclist rides in the adjacent vehicle lane among cars, contradicting the lane’s intended purpose.
The relaxation kit contains bath-only items such as bath salt, bubble bath, and a bath bomb, but the bathroom has only a shower stall and no tub in which to use them.

The phone boasts an oversized multi-lens “MEGA CAMERA,” yet its gallery contains only mundane utility snapshots such as meter readings, receipts, parking locations, and food. The sophisticated camera hardware is humorously wasted on low-key content.
Someone asks to be texted when the other person gets home, implying concern, but then sleeps peacefully beside a muted phone and cannot receive the update.
A punching dummy designed to withstand repeated blows is wrapped in protective tape labeled “CAUTION FRAGILE,” while the unwrapped panel reveals its muscular, robust form.
Cooking, a call from the boss, laundry, and ironing all demand attention, but the person cannot act because a sleeping cat has claimed their lap. The cat humorously takes priority over every chore.
The reusable bottle and recycling symbol suggest eco-consciousness, but it is being refilled from a disposable plastic bottle, undermining that environmental gesture.
The woman recoils from a medical syringe and covers her face, yet calmly undergoes lip piercing and tattooing with other needles. Her fear disappears when needles become fashion tools.
The apparent robot in the left panel is revealed on the right to be a human wearing robotic armor, holding the removed robot helmet under his arm.

The camouflage-painted car looks cleverly concealed, but when it blends into roadside vegetation, another car crashes into it because it is difficult to see. Its concealment feature becomes a safety hazard.

The waiter presents a large covered platter with ceremonial flair, but underneath is only a tiny decorative morsel amid sauce. The grand presentation contrasts comically with the meal's negligible substance.

The man turns the sink faucet and holds out his hand to wash it, but the water unexpectedly pours from the overhead shower onto his head instead. The plumbing control produces a comically misplaced result.

The highly educated elder with broad expertise receives one microphone, while the younger TikTok expert with little academic or life experience attracts a huge press scrum. The joke critiques society's preference for social-media fame over substantive knowledge.

With the bulb off, shadows make the man's torso look muscular and defined; when the bulb is on, the same torso appears smooth and ordinary. The joke is that his physique changes only through lighting and perception.

The elaborate recording studio and its instruments suggest traditional music production, but the right panel reduces composition to clicking a simple digital sequencer of sampled sounds. The humor contrasts sophisticated physical equipment with minimal software-based beat making.
The sneakers look spotless and sparkling while worn, but removing one reveals a visibly dirty sock sole hidden inside. The pristine exterior conceals the grime created during wear.
A luxury pen priced at $2,065 promises refined writing, but it produces an awkward, barely legible signature. The expensive instrument cannot compensate for the user's poor penmanship.

The “MISS UNIVERSE” sash crowns an ordinary Earth woman, while the actual universe contains diverse alien contestants. The joke exposes the pageant title’s absurdly Earth-centered claim to universality.

A potato peeler produces one long, unbroken peel, which the right panel reimagines as the flowing ribbon of a contorted rhythmic gymnast. The mundane kitchen task visually becomes an elaborate athletic performance.
What appears to be a stylish blue pocket square in the suited man's breast pocket is revealed to be a face mask, turning a practical 2020 necessity into formalwear decoration.

The close-up makes the woman’s heel and the sneaker look like a pair standing together. The wider view reveals the sneaker belongs to a short bystander positioned between the woman and the tall man she is actually toasting.
The apparent protruding belly in the left panel looks like excess body weight, but the right panel reveals that the bulge is actually a large snail hidden beneath the shirt.

The man appears to celebrate crossing a finish ribbon under confetti like a champion, but the wider view reveals that his grand daily achievement is merely getting out of bed, with slippers waiting on the floor.
The close-up presents a normal wireless earbud, but the wider view reveals unequal performance: the left earbud has a depleted battery while music plays only through the right one.

The woman refuses a COVID vaccine despite the waiting vial and syringe, yet readily accepts a hyaluronic-acid injection into her lips. Her selective fear of medically administered injections creates the contradiction.
Her fogged glasses initially prevent her from seeing; after removing them, the reveal is that her eyes are closed anyway. Clearing the lenses is pointless if she does not keep her eyes open.

The man imagines himself ceremonially cutting a ribbon under a spotlight, but he is actually cutting through queue barriers to bypass the winding line. His grandiose self-image contrasts with his mundane queue-cutting misconduct.

The pizza appears generously covered with many sausage slices, but lifting the top reveals that the apparent slices are holes exposing a single sausage layer underneath. The abundance is only an illusion.

The impeccably clean suit and elegant champagne glass suggest refined decorum, while the same man later appears drunk on the floor in a torn, stained suit clutching a bottle. His polished appearance collapses into chaotic celebration.

The navigation form treats “Carefree Childhood” as a reachable destination, but the map responds with a seemingly endless route fading into the distance. The joke is that one cannot literally navigate back into the past.
The person chooses a drink labeled organic, gluten-free, non-GMO, and 100% natural, yet simultaneously smokes a cigarette, humorously revealing selective concern for personal health.

The left shows the man properly walking on stairs and cycling on a bike path, while the right reverses this: he cycles down the stairs and walks on the bike path. The swapped uses create the situational absurdity.
The Porsche emblem suggests a luxurious sports car, but the right panel reveals its steering wheel detached and being tossed like a flying disc in a park, puncturing the illusion of luxury.
The close-up suggests a routine mirror selfie inside an elevator, but the wider view reveals the suited man posing in a small exterior lift suspended against a skyscraper.

A factory surveillance camera watches an image of an action camera surfing, while the right panel reveals it drooling enviously amid its dull warehouse reality. The humor contrasts the exciting camera life it imagines with its stationary industrial job.
A man gracefully ducks under a bar while dancing limbo in the YES panel, but uses the same maneuver to slip beneath an airport queue barrier and cut the line in the BUT panel.

The man delights in peeling protective plastic from a remote, yet his suitcase is tightly wrapped in protective film for travel. The humor comes from treating the same packaging as satisfying waste in one context and necessary protection in another.

The left panel shows a single tea bag being taken from the box, while the right shows that same bag being used to brew an absurd tower of mugs. The humor comes from stretching one tea bag far beyond its normal use.
The front of the can advertises “NO SUGAR,” while the other side undercuts that claim with “NO PROBLEM—THERE’S A LOT OF IT,” exposing the misleading packaging.
The bedridden elderly man appears to accept a needed glass of water, but instead uses it with a brush and watercolor palette to paint. The expected act of drinking becomes an artistic one.
A hockey player competes in the “Climate Change Cup,” but the rink has become a grassy golf course, so he swings his hockey stick like a golf club toward a flag.

The left panel frames the man proudly raising a “#1” trophy as proof of victory, while the right reveals him handling identical trophies on a factory production line. The supposedly unique symbol of achievement is merely mass-manufactured merchandise.

The stylish, conspicuously branded wallet looks luxurious from the outside, but when opened it is completely empty. The joke is that buying status-symbol accessories may leave the owner with no money to put inside them.
The tattoo declares “My Life… My Rules,” but the Constitution and physics textbooks show that both social laws and natural laws constrain individual will.

A bird first perches normally atop a glowing streetlamp, but then a bird flies away with the lamp’s bulb forming its body, leaving bare lampposts behind. The scene humorously treats bulbs as if they evolved into birds.
He enters the money-change shop wearing one dollar-sign chain, but emerges burdened with a huge mass of cent-sign chains—apparently receiving 100 cents as literal fashion accessories.
A person dips a chip into guacamole while pretzels lie on the floor, but the dog is humorously seated at the table with the chips and dip while pretzels sit beside it like discarded dog food.

The entryway’s many shoes suggest a large gathering, but they apparently belong to one enormous many-legged guest standing beside the gamer. The apparent crowd is therefore just a deceptive shoe count.

A man painstakingly builds a fragile pyramid of money labeled “BUDGET,” only for a wrecking ball to demolish it and scatter the cash, humorously depicting reckless spending undoing careful financial planning.

Plastic straws are prohibited in the left panel, supposedly to reduce waste, while the right panel displays many individually packaged disposable sampling swabs. The contrast highlights selective concern about single-use plastic.

The luxury-style badge presents the car as prestigious, but the close side view reveals extensive rust and deterioration around the wheel arch. The polished brand image clashes with the vehicle’s shabby physical condition.

The men initially appear to have ordinary hairstyles, but they greet each other by lifting their hairpieces as though tipping hats. The revealed bald heads turn a courteous hat gesture into an absurd wig salute.

Free scissors (YES) vs. scissors sealed in a blister pack whose dashed cut-line requires scissors to open (BUT), creating an inescapable access paradox.

The comic contrasts the mundane task of peeling a potato with a gymnast using the long peel as a rhythmic ribbon, creating a humorous situational incongruity.

The left panel shows what appears to be a classic blue pocket square in a suit breast pocket, but the right panel reveals it is actually a folded surgical face mask being pulled out, subverting the gentleman's accessory trope.

The left panel shows feet close together, implying a couple of similar height, but the right panel reveals the shoes belong to a tall woman and a short man standing between her and her actual tall partner, creating a situational illusion.
The left panel shows a person with what appears to be a large belly, but the right panel reveals it is actually a giant snail shell attached to their back, creating a physical incongruity.

The left panel shows a man celebrating with confetti and a finish-line ribbon like a champion, but the right panel reveals he merely jumped out of bed in his bedroom. The humor comes from treating the mundane act of waking up as a grand athletic victory.

The YES panel shows a person wearing a wireless earbud, implying stereo listening. The BUT panel reveals one earbud has a low battery (dead) while the other still plays music, leaving the listener with only one-sided audio.

The comic highlights the irony of a person refusing a COVID vaccine for health reasons while willingly accepting a hyaluron lip filler injection, revealing a contradiction in their values regarding medical interventions.
In the YES panel, the woman's glasses appear fogged up. In the BUT panel, she removes the glasses to reveal her eyes themselves are foggy/white, showing the problem was her eyes, not the glasses.
The man believes he is performing an important ribbon-cutting ceremony, but the ribbon was merely a queue barrier rope, leaving him still waiting in line like everyone else.

The left panel shows a pizza appearing to have many sausage slices, but the right panel reveals the 'slices' are just holes in the dough with one large sausage underneath, creating a contradiction between appearance and reality.

The comic contrasts the elegant image of a man in a sharp suit holding champagne with the reality of him slumped on the floor, disheveled and holding a beer bottle, highlighting the messy aftermath of celebration.

The navigation app shows a route from 'Current Location' to 'Carefree Childhood,' but the map reveals the path is broken and disconnected, illustrating the impossibility of physically navigating back to a past time period.

The comic contrasts a hand holding a bottle labeled 'organic,' 'gluten-free,' and '100% natural' with the same hand holding a lit cigarette, highlighting the paradox of selective health consciousness.
The man walks up stairs but rides his bike up them, and rides his bike on the bike path but walks on it — he uses the wrong mode of transport for each path, creating a situational contradiction.

The YES panel shows a hand gripping a Porsche steering wheel, implying luxury driving. The BUT panel reveals the wheel is being thrown as a frisbee in a park, subverting the expectation of actual Porsche ownership.

The left panel shows what appears to be a casual mirror selfie in an elevator, but the right panel reveals the man is actually standing on a tiny outdoor platform photographing his reflection in a building window.

A security camera in a warehouse is shown gazing at a surfing poster, then drooling water as if fantasizing about surfing. The humor comes from personifying the camera with human desires that contradict its stationary, industrial reality.

The left panel shows a man seemingly collapsed under a queue barrier, but the right panel reveals he is deliberately bending backward to cut in line. The humor comes from the situational misdirection between appearing unconscious and actually queue-jumping.

The man is emotionally crying over his TV remote in the left panel, then in the right panel he is shown traveling with a suitcase that resembles the remote, absurdly taking his beloved remote with him as luggage.

The YES panel shows a single tea bag and one mug, implying a standard cup of tea. The BUT panel reveals the person using that single tea bag to brew a massive stack of mugs, creating a situational contradiction of stretching one bag far beyond its intended use.

The left panel shows a soda can labeled 'NO SUGAR,' but the right panel reveals the full text: 'NO SUGAR? NO PROBLEM THERE'S A LOT OF IT,' exposing a misleading health claim through the hidden side of the label.
The elderly patient in bed is handed a glass of water presumably for drinking, but instead uses it to mix watercolor paints, subverting the caregiving premise with an artistic twist.
The hockey player wears a 'Climate Change Cup' jersey but is forced to play golf on grass because climate change melted the ice rink, turning a hockey game into a golf game.

The left panel shows a person triumphantly holding a '#1' trophy, implying personal achievement. The right panel reveals the same person packing identical mass-produced trophies in a factory, undermining the trophy's meaning as a symbol of unique victory.

The comic contrasts a fancy, branded luxury wallet in the first panel with the revelation in the second panel that it is completely empty, highlighting the irony of owning an expensive accessory but having no money to put in it.

The person's tattoo declares 'My Life... My Rules...' but the right panel reveals their life is actually governed by external forces: the Constitution, laws of physics, astronomy, justice, and law enforcement.

The YES panel shows a pigeon perched on a lamppost light. The BUT panel reveals pigeons whose bodies end in lightbulbs, flying and perching on branches — they have become the light sources themselves, a absurd situational evolution.

The man enters a '$$$ CHANGE' currency exchange shop wearing one dollar-sign chain, but exits literally covered in 'C'-shaped chains. The humor is a visual pun on 'change' being interpreted as physical chains rather than currency.

The left panel shows a human dipping a pretzel into a bowl of dip, while the right panel reveals a dog under the table dipping its paw into its own small bowl of the same dip, humorously mimicking the human's snack time.
The left panel shows many shoes by the door, implying a crowded party, but the right panel reveals only one person and a giant multi-legged creature, explaining the numerous shoes.

The comic contrasts the careful, fragile construction of a personal budget with its sudden destruction by the massive, unavoidable expense of Christmas, represented by the giant ornament wrecking ball.

The left panel shows a prohibition sign banning plastic straws, while the right panel shows a container overflowing with disposable plastic sampling swabs. The humor lies in society's selective environmental scrutiny—banning straws while mass-producing disposable swabs.
The left panel shows a prestigious brand emblem on a car suggesting luxury, but the right panel reveals the car is old, rusty, and dilapidated, contradicting the brand's image.

Two men greet each other by tipping their 'hats,' but the hats are actually their own hairpieces, revealing they are both bald underneath. The polite gesture of hat-tipping becomes absurd when the 'hats' are their own hair.
